title: Cosmic ice sculptures: dust pillars in the Carina Nebula
caption: Dust pillars in the Carina Nebula, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Carina Nebula · constellation Carina · about 7500 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble Heritage Project (STScI/AURA). Acknowledgment: M. Livio (STScI) and N. Smith (University of California, Berkeley, USA)

recognition.text: Published in the ESA/Hubble image archive. No published rating.

story: Tall pillars of cold hydrogen and dust rise in the Carina Nebula in this Hubble picture, each one about a light-year high. Like ice cream melting out of shape on a hot summer day, they are being worn away, in this case by radiation from massive stars.

Fierce stellar winds and strong radiation from those stars are carving away at cold molecular clouds, sculpting the surrounding nebula into strange, fantasy-like forms. Inside these dense structures, new stars may form.

The Carina Nebula lies in the southern constellation Carina, an estimated 7,500 light-years away. Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys built this composite from two sets of observations. The 2005 data record hydrogen light, given off by hydrogen atoms, and the 2010 data record oxygen light, given off by oxygen atoms.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (5.15 x 3.04 arcminutes) and distance (7500 light years), the frame spans roughly 11 × 6.6 light-years. Its light set out about 7,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys recorded the pillars through narrow filters that isolate light from glowing hydrogen and oxygen. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The narrow filters isolate light from single chemical elements, and the nebula is far too faint for the eye to see in this detail.

explore: The two filters used pick out narrow wavelengths, one at 502 nanometers for glowing oxygen and one at 658 nanometers for hydrogen and nitrogen. The picture is credited to the Hubble Heritage Project, with thanks to M. Livio and N. Smith.
alt: Tall pillars of cold hydrogen gas and dust in the Carina Nebula.
